newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Saudi Aramco in talks with 13 Asian naphtha buyers.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Aramco in talks with 13 Asian naphtha buyers.

text.p: Saudi Aramco has shortlisted thirteen companies, including nine from Japan, to negotiate the sale of up to 3.9 million tonnes of naphtha, industry sources said on Friday.
Both sides would be holding term talks in Singapore from Monday to Thursday to finalise details for the sale of the Saudi term naphtha for lifting between July and December 1997, they said.

In the term talks, Saudi Aramco is expected to offer 2.9 million tonnes of light naphtha for lifting from Ras Tanura and a total of 1.3 million tonnes of full range naphtha -- 800,000 tonnes from Jubail and 500,000 tonnes from Rabigh.

Buyers in Japan and Singapore told Reuters that Saudi Aramco had set a target premia of $17.00 per tonne over Aramco's A-180 paraffinic naphtha grade compared to the $6.50 premium it received for its January to June 1997 contract.
Japanese term lifters considered the price to be too high and most have submitted bids at premiums of between $14-$15 per tonne.

Traders in Singapore said, outside Japan, three of the shortlisted companies - Brazil's Petrobras, South Korea's Hyundai and India's Reliance have submitted bids $17 per tonne premium, similar to Saudi's offer.

Traders said Hyundai would be scheduled to have talks with Saudi on the first day of negotiations. They said the South Korean firm is likely to accept Saudi Aramco's offer price as the firm is considering expanding its naphtha cracker capacity later this year.
Hyundai Petrochemical currently has a 400,000 tonnes a year naphtha cracker.
Some traders said they fear that if Hyundai accepts Saudi's offer price, the rest of the buyers would have to follow suit as Aramco sets only one standard price for its naphtha sale.

"These companies are likely to get their volumes, but we think we cannot move up to meet that price, considering current market conditions, I hope the Saudi could edge lower," said a Japanese term lifter.
Other traders also hope that the current weakness would work in their favour.

Naphtha prices in the spot market has been falling since late April. Some traders estimated that about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes of naphtha have been shipped to Asia since the arbitrage window from Europe opened in March.

While Saudi Aramco may ease its offer prices, it is unlikely to move below Kuwait's $13.50 premium, traders said. Earlier this year, Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) was able to clinch a term price of $13.50 per tonne over mean of Middle East quotes, due to growing petrochemical demand in Asia.
Aramco and KPC are the largest exports of Middle East naphtha to Asia and their pricing policies, though based on different market formulas, often mirror each other.
The remaining companies that are shortlisted includes Petrochemical Corporation of Singapore, Japan's Marubeni Corp, Mitsui, Mitsubishi Chemical, Kanematsu Itochu Corp, Sumitomo Corp.
With contribution from Kiyoshi Tanaka in Tokyo.
